intro: The best AI note taker for lectures is LessonScriptor, a free Chrome extension that transcribes any video playing in a browser tab, live or recorded, and turns it into an editable transcript. Most well-known AI note takers, Otter.ai and Fireflies among them, are built to join a live meeting as a bot. That's a different job from transcribing a recorded lecture, a YouTube tutorial, or a video on a university platform, which is what most students actually need. This guide compares the main options on the thing that matters for lecture notes: does it work on a recording, not just a live call.

sections.h2: What is an AI note taker, and which kind do students need?
sections.body:
AI note takers fall into two categories. The first is meeting bots, tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies that join a Zoom or Google Meet call as a participant and record what's said. They're built for live meetings and work well for that, but they can't join a lecture that's already recorded, or transcribe a YouTube video.

The second category is browser-based transcription, tools like LessonScriptor that capture audio from whatever is playing in a Chrome tab, whether that's a live call or a recorded video. For lectures specifically, most of which are recorded, on Panopto, Canvas, YouTube, or a university's own platform, this is the category that actually helps.

sections.h2: Why LessonScriptor works better for lecture notes
sections.body:
The gap with meeting-bot tools isn't accuracy, it's coverage. A student's week is mostly recorded content: a professor's Panopto capture, a YouTube explainer assigned as homework, a Coursera video. A tool built to join live calls simply doesn't run on any of that.

LessonScriptor transcribes whatever is playing in the tab, live class or recorded video, with the same free mode and no monthly limit. The transcript is editable while it builds, so most of the tidying, highlighting the key line, bolding a term, adding a header, happens before the video even ends.

Writing and listening at the same time splits attention in a way that's especially hard with ADHD. Handing the writing over to a transcript that builds itself removes that split entirely, leaving working memory free to just follow the lecture.

items.q: What's the best free AI note taker for students?
items.a: LessonScriptor's free mode has no account requirement and no monthly cap, and works on both live classes and recorded lecture videos. Meeting-bot tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies have free tiers too, but they're built for live meetings only.

items.q: Does an AI note taker work on recorded lectures, not just live calls?
items.a: It depends on the tool. Meeting bots (Otter.ai, Fireflies) join live calls as a participant and can't transcribe something already recorded. LessonScriptor transcribes any video playing in a Chrome tab, live or recorded.

items.q: Do I need an account to use LessonScriptor?
items.a: No. Free mode has no signup at all. If you buy an AI mode credit pack for better accuracy, you get a license key by email, no account or login.

items.q: Is student or lecture audio sent anywhere?
items.a: In free mode, nothing leaves your computer, transcription runs locally through your browser's speech engine. In AI mode, audio is sent to a cloud transcription model in short chunks and is not stored.

items.q: Which AI note taker supports the most languages?
items.a: Notta covers the widest range at 50+ languages. LessonScriptor supports 14, including French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Arabic and Hindi, which covers most university lecture languages.
